title: Observability & resilience — OTel, latency, Polly
exp: Logs + metrics + traces, correlated by trace id. Plus timeouts, retries, and circuit breakers used correctly.
pts: Latency checklist: P95/P99, traces, ThreadPool/GC counters, N+1, sync-over-async.
Polly: timeout, retry (transient only), circuit breaker, bulkhead — retries must be idempotent.
Don't log secrets; prefer structured Serilog properties.

r: Deep dive into Day 11 runtime execution mechanics and threading constraints.
Focus on zero-allocation and lock-free patterns where applicable.
High concurrency contention or unexpected resource exhaustion under load.
Implement resilient backpressure, retries, and circuit breakers.
Balancing low latency, developer ergonomics, and system consistency.
Always state operational cost and complexity trade-offs.

qa.q: How do you debug increasing API latency over days?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Check metrics (P95, errors, dependency times), distributed traces for slow spans, runtime counters (thread pool queue, GC), recent deploys/config, and classics: N+1, missing index, sync-over-async, cache stampede, chatty logging.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Boxing allocates a System.Object header (16 bytes on x64) on the managed heap and copies the value type bytes into it. Span<T> is a ref struct allocated strictly on the execution stack, providing contiguous memory access without heap allocation or array copying.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Boxing inside a high-throughput loop generates thousands of ephemeral Gen 0 objects, triggering frequent GC pauses and thread pool delays. Fix: use generic collection interfaces (IList<T>) and Span<T>/Memory<T> for byte slicing.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Span<T> provides zero-allocation performance, but ref struct rules forbid storing it on the heap, as class fields, or across async await points (where Memory<T> must be used).

qa.q: When should a retry policy NOT retry?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** On non-transient errors (400 validation, 401/403), non-idempotent POSTs without idempotency keys, and after a circuit is open. Retry timeouts/5xx/connection resets with jittered backoff.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Operating When should a retry policy NOT retry? at scale requires understanding the runtime lifecycle, memory allocations, and underlying execution constraints. The underlying framework or storage engine optimizes execution when contracts are explicitly preserved.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Un-handled edge cases in When should a retry policy NOT retry? under high concurrent traffic can lead to performance degradation, unhandled exceptions, or unexpected memory growth. Always enforce defensive validation and error handling.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Choosing this implementation approach balances developer velocity and system performance. Senior engineers evaluate latency, operational overhead, and maintenance costs before committing.
